overview: This Senate resolution designates September 2025 as National Child Awareness Month. It aims to promote awareness of charities and youth-serving organizations that provide children with health care, social services, education, arts, sports and other support, and recognizes their work as critical to the country's future. It highlights the needs of children and youth who have experienced homelessness, are in foster care, are at risk of child sex trafficking, have been affected by violence or trauma, or have serious physical or mental health needs. The Senate adopted it by unanimous consent on September 19, 2025.
for: Supporters say the designation draws attention to the needs of vulnerable children and encourages support for the groups that serve them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for children's services.
